title: Workspace manifest hygiene: undeclared and unused @moe dependencies
description: Objective: make workspace manifests match real imports. MEASURED at HEAD 7183c04 (grep of imports vs package.json) on 2026-08-09: (1) packages/scheduler imports @moe/contracts but does not declare it - works only via hoisting; add the workspace dependency. (2) apps/control-room test files import @moe/store and @moe/testkit undeclared; add both as devDependencies. (3) packages/coordination declares @moe/core and never imports it; remove the entry. (4) pnpm-workspace.yaml lists adapters/* but the directory does not exist; the design reserves adapters/* for external integration boundaries, so KEEP the glob and add a one-line comment marking it reserved - removing it would be a design deviation needing a governor decision. NOT in scope: version bumps, any dependency beyond the three named, code changes. Owned paths: packages/scheduler/package.json, apps/control-room/package.json, packages/coordination/package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml (regeneration only). Verification: pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test.
definitionOfDone: scheduler declares @moe/contracts; control-room declares @moe/store and @moe/testkit as devDependencies; coordination no longer declares @moe/core; lockfile regenerated
adapters/* glob kept with a reserved-comment, or an explicit governor decision recorded for its removal
pnpm install, pnpm typecheck and pnpm test all exit 0

The corrected scope is exactly three changes and nothing more: (a) remove @moe/core from packages/coordination/package.json, (b) regenerate the lockfile, (c) add a one-line reserved comment to the adapters/* entry in pnpm-workspace.yaml. DO NOT ADD ANY DEPENDENCY TO ANY PACKAGE. Specifically: do NOT add @moe/contracts to packages/scheduler, and do NOT add @moe/store or @moe/testkit to apps/control-room. The governor's note is explicit that a diff doing either is a REJECTION rather than compliance. Re-confirm the one surviving claim yourself in one command before editing -- `git grep -nE 'from "@moe/core"' HEAD -- packages/coordination/src` must return ZERO hits while packages/coordination/package.json declares it. This step edits nothing; affectedFiles is intentionally empty so read-only files do not count against the plan's file budget.

implementationPlan.description: Regenerate the lockfile, guarding against the one hazard that makes this step unsafe in a shared working directory. pnpm-lock.yaml is a WHOLE-WORKSPACE artifact: any foreign manifest edit that happens to be dirty when install runs gets baked into the lock and lands in this task's commit. So first run `git status --porcelain -- '*package.json' 'pnpm-lock.yaml' pnpm-workspace.yaml` and confirm the ONLY dirty manifest is packages/coordination/package.json. If any other package.json is dirty, stop and wait for its owner rather than regenerating over it -- packages/store/package.json was dirty from a foreign task earlier today, so this is a live hazard and not a hypothetical. Then run `pnpm install`, and inspect the resulting `git diff -- pnpm-lock.yaml`: it should show the removal of the coordination -> @moe/core edge and nothing else. A lockfile diff touching unrelated packages means a foreign manifest was picked up; discard and retry when the tree is clean.

Verify, then commit by pathspec. Run the exact verification command `pnpm install && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`. The typecheck leg is the one that matters here: it is what would catch a removal that was actually load-bearing, because if anything in packages/coordination did import @moe/core the removal would surface as an unresolved module rather than as a silent runtime failure later. Both other legs are repo-wide in a shared working directory, so if either is red apply the path-attributed baseline rail -- record failures at the merge-base, then at HEAD, and complete only if the delta intersected with this task's owned paths (packages/coordination/package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml) is EMPTY, disclosing any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing file paths rather than hiding it or claiming a green it did not get. Then confirm with `git status --porcelain` that no foreign path is staged and commit by explicit pathspec only: `git commit -- packages/coordination/package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-lock.yaml`. Verify with `git show --stat` that exactly those three files landed. In the completion note, state explicitly that the scheduler and control-room clauses of the stored DoD item 1 were struck by the governor at 14:56Z and were deliberately NOT implemented, and quote the two measurements that falsified them, so QA reads the corrected scope rather than the stale DoD text.

comments.content:
ARCHITECT RE-MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-09. Description measured at HEAD 7183c04; I measured at a423722/7d9efc9. Three of four claims hold. Claim 2 is falsified and DoD item 1 requires it, so this is BLOCKED pending a one-line DoD amendment. Full evidence below.

METHOD NOTE: a bare `grep -rhoE '@moe/[a-z-]+'` gives the wrong answer here, because these packages discuss their own dependency policy in prose comments and one app plants fake import strings as test fixtures. Every count below is from `grep -rnoE "(from|import|mock|require)\s*\(?\s*[\"']@moe/[a-z-]+"` — real specifiers only — cross-checked against an unfiltered grep of the whole directory.

CLAIM 1 — CONFIRMED, with a correction to the fix shape.
`packages/scheduler/src` real external specifiers: `from "@moe/contracts"` x1. `packages/scheduler/package.json` has NO dependencies and NO devDependencies field at all — it is `{}`, so the worker must CREATE `dependencies`, not append to it. Add only `"@moe/contracts": "workspace:*"`.
DO NOT ALSO ADD @moe/core. A raw grep shows `@moe/core` in packages/scheduler/src, but both hits are comments stating the opposite: budget-measurement.ts:15 "No @moe/core or @moe/contracts import — the projected budget fact mirrors..." and budget-reservation.ts:13 "@moe/core is not imported by design and no policy is re-evaluated". Adding it would break a documented design boundary.
Also observed, out of scope, flagged only: `from "@moe/scheduler"` x7 inside its own src (self-referential package-root imports, e.g. index-surface.test.ts). That resolves through the pnpm self-link and is not a manifest defect; not planning it.

CLAIM 2 — FALSIFIED. DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS WRITTEN.
`@moe/store` and `@moe/testkit` have ZERO real import specifiers anywhere in apps/control-room. Every occurrence is a ban artifact:
- evidence/evidence-timeline-ban.test.ts:82 — `"@moe/store"` is an entry in `BANNED_PACKAGES`, alongside @moe/contracts, @moe/coordination and @moe/core. The comment above it at :74 states the intent: these packages own authority and "reaching for one would give this app a second path to daemon truth beside the gated client".
- evidence-timeline-ban.test.ts:221 — a PLANTED fixture string, ``const planted = `import { CURSOR_GAP } from "@moe/store/subscriptions";` ``, synthesized to prove the ban detector fires.
- evidence-timeline-ban.test.ts:225 — the assertion that the detector caught it.
- scaffold.test.tsx:269 — `@moe/testkit/foundation/model.js` inside a `heldOutImport.test(...)` regex assertion, again a held-out import, not an import.
Declared in apps/control-room/package.json: @moe/contracts, @moe/control-room-client, @moe/control-room-model. Real specifiers: @moe/contracts x38, @moe/control-room-client x4, @moe/control-room-model x6. The manifest already matches the imports exactly. There is nothing to fix.
Adding @moe/store and @moe/testkit as devDependencies would declare two packages nothing imports — creating precisely the defect claim 3 exists to remove, and inverting this task's stated objective, "make workspace manifests match real imports".

CLAIM 3 — CONFIRMED EXACTLY.
packages/coordination real specifiers (src + tests): @moe/contracts x5, @moe/store x4. Declares @moe/contracts, @moe/core, @moe/store. `@moe/core` is declared and never imported. Remove it.

CLAIM 4 — CONFIRMED.
pnpm-workspace.yaml lists `apps/*`, `adapters/*`, `packages/*`. `ls -d adapters` -> "No such file or directory". Keep the glob, add the reserved comment, as the description directs.

REQUESTED DoD AMENDMENT — item 1, replace:
  "scheduler declares @moe/contracts; control-room declares @moe/store and @moe/testkit as devDependencies; coordination no longer declares @moe/core; lockfile regenerated"
with:
  "scheduler declares @moe/contracts; coordination no longer declares @moe/core; apps/control-room/package.json is unchanged and the plan records why; lockfile regenerated"
Items 2 and 3 need no change. With that amendment this is a clean 4-5 step task and I will plan it immediately.

INCIDENTAL, FOR WHOEVER PLANS IT: at 14:38Z apps/daemon/package.json and two src files were staged-modified in the shared index, which would have polluted a `pnpm install` lockfile regeneration. As of HEAD 7d9efc9 that has cleared — no manifest or lockfile path is dirty, and only recovery/continuation-service.ts (task-5855a9c6, legitimately WORKING) remains modified under apps/daemon. Re-check `git status --porcelain -- '*package.json' 'pnpm-lock.yaml'` immediately before running install, because the lock is a whole-workspace artifact and any foreign manifest edit present at that moment gets baked in.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:

That was the right call and it is why the task came back with a governor-recorded correction instead of a silent scope change. The same reasoning now applies in reverse: with the governor's correction on the record, the plan can safely omit the struck clauses, and step 5 requires the worker to restate the correction in the completion note so QA reads the corrected scope rather than the stale DoD text.

REMOVING THE GLOB. Rejected, twice, and the second time by the governor explicitly. An empty adapters/ directory looks like dead config, but the design reserves adapters/* for external integration boundaries and task-9fd52b41 owns adapters/jetbrains/**. Removing it would be a design deviation requiring a governor decision, and it would break the next task to populate that path. The comment exists so the next person to notice the empty directory finds the answer in the file rather than re-opening the question.

FIXING THE SCHEDULER MANIFEST HERE ANYWAY. Rejected. packages/scheduler/package.json is genuinely {} with no dependencies field, which looks like a defect worth fixing while nearby. But nothing in scheduler currently imports across a package boundary, so there is nothing to declare -- adding an entry would create the very defect this task removes from coordination. Separately, task-cda6bddf4e6e464e895c696e79bc9784 (Same-bug circuit breaker) adds a genuine @moe/context import to scheduler and its plan correctly creates the dependencies field there. With the scheduler clause struck from this task, that collision no longer exists and the two tasks are now file-disjoint.

A FORMATTING OR VERSION SWEEP WHILE IN THE FILES. Rejected as scope creep. The description's NOT-in-scope line rules out version bumps and any dependency beyond the named ones, and a one-line diff is what makes this reviewable.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE STALE DoD IS THE PRIMARY RISK ON THIS TASK, and it has already bitten twice. A worker who reads definitionOfDone and not reopenReason will add two or three dependencies that nothing imports, which is a rejection. Step 1 exists solely to force reading the correction first, and step 5 makes the worker restate it in the completion note.

2. THE FIXTURE TRAP THAT CAUSED ALL OF THIS. Both false claims came from a grep counting ban-test fixtures and prose comments as imports. If the worker re-measures anything here, use a specifier-shaped pattern (`from "@moe/..."`), then OPEN each hit and check whether it sits inside a fixture table, a comment, or a quoted string. In this repo a hit inside a file named *-ban.test.* or *package-boundary.test.* is evidence AGAINST the dependency, not for it. I made exactly this mistake on scheduler after having already written up the pattern for control-room.

3. LOCKFILE CONTAMINATION. `pnpm install` regenerates a whole-workspace artifact. If a foreign package.json is dirty at that moment its changes land in this task's lockfile diff and then in this task's commit. Gate on `git status --porcelain -- '*package.json'` immediately before install, and inspect the lockfile diff afterwards -- it should show only the coordination -> @moe/core edge disappearing.

4. REPO-WIDE VERIFICATION LEGS IN A SHARED TREE. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` are repo-wide and several agents are active. Attribute red by path before treating it as this task's defect, and disclose foreign red verbatim rather than hiding it or fabricating a green.

5. LOW RISK OF REAL BREAKAGE. This is a three-file, largely subtractive change. The one way it could be wrong is if @moe/core were imported somewhere I did not look; `pnpm typecheck` is the leg that would catch it, which is why step 5 calls it out specifically rather than treating all three legs as interchangeable.
